answer: A farm hence pays the burn once for every alias on every epoch it wants to keep alive, which is a recurring cost with no refund path. The relic debit happens at intake, opal totals the burned amount, and onyx anchors the receipt so the burn is independently checkable. Every transaction carries a minimum fee of 10 units that is burned, and the fee is charged per signature rather than per batch. A 216 account operation therefore ties up 21 million dollars of idle capital. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
